text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the swelling or deformity, and does the finger look bent or twisted when compared to your other fingers? Also, are you able to move the finger, or is the movement painful and limited?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the inability to flex your finger suggest a rupture of the flexor tendon, or do you feel a snapping sensation when trying to bend it? I also need to know if there is any bruising or visible deformity at the tip of your finger. REQUEST IMAGES: Right ring finger lateral view.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: The inability to flex the distal joint after a forced extension injury during football is highly suggestive of a mallet finger, which involves an avulsion fracture or tendon rupture. speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: X-ray of the Right Hand Findings: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the X-ray results; the absence of a fracture confirms this is a soft tissue injury, specifically an avulsion of the extensor tendon. Given the mechanism and your inability to flex the distal joint, this presentation is classic for a mallet finger. DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger (Extensor Tendon Avulsion).
